title: Student Loans: UGH!
summary: Josh and Chuck (with guest producer Dave) explain student loans in the US: how the debt built up since the Obama-era expansion of higher education access around 2010, federal loan types (direct subsidized, direct unsubsidized, direct PLUS), cost-of-attendance borrowing limits, private loans and their fixed versus variable rates, repayment options (deferment, forbearance, income-driven plans, consolidation/refinancing), Public Service Loan Forgiveness and the tax consequences of forgiveness, default and rehabilitation, for-profit and online college risks, the "sheepskin effect," securitization of student loans, a proposal to use 401(k) money to repay loans, and listener mail corrections.

segments.title: Opening banter and personal college funding stories
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode as a public service piece, joke about its dryness, and share personal stories about paying for college, including selling a camper and the Georgia HOPE grant.

segments.title: Rising college costs and the changed value of debt
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the growth of student loan debt, the Obama-era initiative that expanded access, and how debt today differs from older mortgage-style debt. They also discuss parents who did not save for college.

segments.title: Federal student loan types
segments.summary: The hosts explain the federal loan categories: direct subsidized loans, where the Department of Education covers interest in certain periods and only undergraduates qualify; direct unsubsidized loans; and direct PLUS loans for parents and graduate students.

segments.title: Cost of attendance and over-borrowing
segments.summary: The hosts explain how cost of attendance sets loan limits and how borrowing the full amount can mean paying interest on unneeded money. They advise borrowing only what is needed and note that schools may hold leftover funds.

segments.title: College choice, cost and degree value
segments.summary: The hosts advise choosing an affordable school, argue that attending an out-of-state public school is a poor value, and discuss how heavy debt and liberal arts degrees can limit life choices.

segments.title: Private student loans
segments.summary: The hosts compare private lenders with federal loans. Private lenders may offer perks but may deny applicants, may rely on co-signers, and may offer variable rates tied to LIBOR and prime that can rise over time. Private loans are typically paid to the school.

segments.title: Repayment options: deferment, interest payments, and federal plans
segments.summary: The hosts describe deferment, immediate repayment, interest-only payments, standard and extended federal repayment terms, and consolidation versus refinancing. They discuss income-driven plans such as REPAYE, which set payments as a share of discretionary income.

segments.title: Public Service Loan Forgiveness and forgiveness tax
segments.summary: The hosts explain Public Service Loan Forgiveness, which requires 120 qualifying payments and full-time work for a qualifying nonpartisan government or nonprofit employer. They also explain that other forgiveness after long repayment may count as taxable income.

segments.title: Default, delinquency, forbearance and rehabilitation
segments.summary: The hosts explain delinquency, default after 270 days, aggressive collection calls, and the drawbacks of forbearance. They describe loan rehabilitation as a way to recover from default and note the debt bubble, securitization of loans, and the some-college problem.

segments.title: 401(k) proposal and data sharing
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a proposal by Rand Paul to let people withdraw 401(k) money penalty-free to repay student loans and criticize the lack of federal data on school outcomes.

segments.title: Listener mail corrections and sign-off
segments.summary: Two listener emails correct the pronunciation of crepuscular and Tagalog, and the hosts sign off.
